“A maid of the queen's went out by night into the forest, and there she saw him riding round a great fire on a cooking spoon … and at the last the little man flew out of the window on the cooking spoon.”
The Grimms' notes to Rumpelstiltskin, first edition, 1812
Something long and carved leans in the back of the hearth, behind the embers. It will not come loose for someone who has not signed in.
Something long and carved leans in the back of the hearth. It is stuck fast in the soot: it will come loose after the Keeper's next update.
The spoon of the little man himself, where he left it when he flew down Poe's chimney.

Only ashes, and a long scrape in the soot where something was drawn out. Someone reached in before you. There is only one, and it is theirs.

You reach in past the embers. They do not burn. Your hand closes on a carved handle, warm as a loaf, and out it comes: a cooking spoon longer than you are tall, its bowl heaped with straw that glows like gold, a little spinning wheel lashed to its neck, and on the end of the handle a grinning carved face in a pointed cap.
There is only one in all the worlds.
It is yours for good, and can never be sold or traded

A great carved beechwood cooking spoon, longer than a man, its bowl heaped with straw that glows like gold. A little spinning wheel turns at its neck and streams a gold thread behind; the knob of its handle is the little man's own grinning face. In the Grimms' first edition (1812) he rides it round a great fire in the forest, and at the last flies out of the window on it.
Pace 4.2 times a walk, and it flies.
There is only one. It can never be sold, traded or given.
